title: Troubleshooting Guide
description: Solutions to common HP OMEN laptop issues, including performance drops, overheating, keyboard/touchpad problems, and hardware glitches.

blocks.content: If you're experiencing low FPS, stuttering, or the laptop feels slow, try these fixes in order:

items: Check power brick AC cord - Push it in HARD. OMEN cables tend to become loose, causing stuttering due to unstable power
Verify you're plugged in - Running on battery significantly limits performance
Check temperatures - Max is 100°C for CPU and 87°C for GPU (2019-2024 OMENs). Higher temps cause throttling. Clean and repaste if needed
Reinstall graphics drivers - Use DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) to clean install both integrated AND discrete GPU drivers from HP Support website
Update drivers after verification - HP drivers may be outdated but stable. Update to latest only after confirming basic functionality

blocks.title: DDU Clean Install
blocks.content: Download DDU from https://www.guru3d.com/download/display-driver-uninstaller-download/. Boot into Safe Mode, run DDU to remove all GPU drivers, then install fresh drivers.
AMD OMEN laptops may experience random stuttering. Try these platform-specific fixes:

items: Turn off TPM - Having TPM enabled causes random stuttering on certain models
Update BIOS - Download latest from HP Support website
Update BIOS - Essential for Windows 11 compatibility
Consider downgrading to Windows 10 if issues persist

blocks.title: This is Normal
blocks.content: Loud fans during gaming are completely normal for gaming laptops. They will sound like a vacuum cleaner or jet engine - this is expected behavior!

items: Use manual fan control in OMEN Gaming Hub (supported models)
Modify the fan curve in OGH for a quieter profile
Use headphones while gaming
Find ways to lower your temps (elevate laptop, cooling pad, repaste)

blocks.title: Abnormal Sounds
blocks.content: If fans make whiny, grinding, or clicking sounds (not just loud whooshing), this indicates a hardware problem. Take your laptop to a service center.
Expected battery life is 4-14 hours depending on model and workload. If you're getting less than 4 hours:

items: Intel models: Switch to Hybrid Mode in OGH graphics settings or BIOS
AMD & Intel: DDU and reinstall BOTH iGPU and dGPU drivers from HP Support
Check GPU activity: NVIDIA Control Panel → Desktop → Show GPU Activity in notification area
Disable hardware acceleration in apps running on dGPU (it's on by default)
Disable NVIDIA App overlay: Settings → Scroll down → Uncheck 'In-Game Overlay'
Uninstall Radeon Settings Lite if installed (keeps GPU awake)
Use HWiNFO: Enable 'Disable wake GPU' in settings, verify idle draw is -6 to -9 watts

blocks.title: Windows 11 Battery Issues
blocks.content: Windows 11 can cause worse battery life because HP drivers aren't 100% compatible. If nothing else works, consider downgrading to Windows 10.
If keys stop working when held down but work when re-pressed:

items: Go to Windows Update → Check for updates
Click 'Optional updates' → Drivers → Keyboard
Download and install the keyboard update
Make sure you're on the latest BIOS version

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: After updating, the keyboard driver may still appear in optional updates - this is normal. Check Update History to confirm it was installed.
This usually means you accidentally pressed the lock keys:

items: F11: Locks/Unlocks the Windows key
F12: Locks/Unlocks the Touchpad
Press the key again (or Fn+F11/F12) to re-enable

steps.title: OMEN Command Center Button Not Working

blocks.content: To fix the OMEN button on your keyboard:

items: Search for 'Apps & Features' in Windows and open it
Scroll down to find 'OMEN Gaming Hub'
Click on it, then click 'Advanced options'
Scroll down and click the 'Repair' button
The OMEN button should now work

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: If you've disabled OGH from startup apps, the button won't work until you manually open OGH at least once after booting.
If your OMEN 15 EK series drops below base clock after sustained use, impacting FPS:

items: Download and open ThrottleStop
Go to TPL window and UNCHECK 'Disable Power Limit Control' if checked
Set Long PL1 value to 55-60W
Click Apply and go to FIVR
Enable 'Disable and Lock Turbo Ratio Limits'
Check 'Save and Apply Voltages after pressing OK'
Click OK

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: You can also set EPP to 0 for constant full turbo. Open ThrottleStop whenever you encounter this issue. This may increase battery drain.

steps.title: VBS Error in OGH / XTU / ThrottleStop

blocks.content: Windows 11 enables Virtualization Based Security by default, which can cause errors in OMEN Gaming Hub, Intel XTU, and ThrottleStop.

items: Search for 'Core Isolation' in Start menu
Turn off 'Memory Integrity'
If you've used WSL2 or Hyper-V, remove them from 'Additional Features'
If still not working, disable Virtualization in BIOS
